name: A blank field is zero; a figure that could not be worked out is unknown
why: The two kinds of missing, side by side. Collapsing them in either direction is the mistake: treat unknown as zero and a runway of `cash / burn` on a plan with no costs yet reads as nought months, which is alarming and wrong; treat blank as unknown and every total on a half-filled record goes empty.

cases.why: The ordinary case, so the file says what normal looks like before it says what the corners are.
A record with no costs has costs of nothing. The total is the revenue, not blank.
Absorbed in a product too, which is the direction that surprises people: nothing times two is nothing, so a blank multiplicand takes the whole term to zero rather than to unknown.
Division by a blank is the first unknown. A blank divisor reads as zero, and dividing by zero has no answer — so this is NOT `100 / 0 = 0`.
And division by an explicit zero, in case an implementation special-cases the blank rather than the zero.
Unknown SPREADS, which is the property a blank does not have. Adding one to something nobody knows still leaves nobody knowing it.
Through multiplication as well. Zero times unknown is not zero — the multiplication is not short-circuited, because the point is that the figure was never worked out.

Two INTEGER columns do decimal arithmetic. 100 / 8 is 12.5, not 12: truncating at each step would disagree with the platform, and would make the answer depend on how the author happened to split the expression.
Nothing done yet is nought per cent, not blank.
No tasks at all is not nought per cent — nobody knows what the progress is, and a project showing 0% because it is empty reads as a project in trouble.
